newsitem.title: CHINA: China takes down HK handover clock in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: China takes down HK handover clock in Beijing.

text.p: China has dismantled the huge digital clock that for 925 days stood in Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing, counting down the seconds to the recovery of Hong Kong from Britain on July 1, state media said on Wednesday.

The clock will be removed to a site on the Great Wall on the outskirts of the Chinese capital. A smaller model, just 156th the size of the original, will go on display in the Chinese Revolutionary Museum on the side of the square, the China Daily said.

A new clock will be put in the same place on the square on December 20, 1997, exactly two years before China resumes sovereignty over Macau, to count down the seconds to the handover of the Portuguese colony, the newspaper said.

"We have finished the design of circuits, and now we are thinking of a different appearance for the new countdown clock," it quoted Xi Guojin, deputy editor of Chinese Top Brands Magazine, as saying. The magazine is in charge of building the clock.
